name: CodeSpace
tagline: A VS Code-style developer workbench, custom-built in C# on Uno
summary: CodeSpace brings a familiar activity bar, explorer, command center, editor groups and bottom panel to a native Uno Platform / C# application. The editor, highlighting, file tree, icons, docking model and composition are all custom-built, with no Monaco, Electron or embedded VS Code workbench. A persistent AVL-rope text engine, Skia renderer and experimental VSIX extension host are packaged as independently reusable libraries.

heroStats.label: less raster time in the CPU text fixture

highlights.title: Custom editor, no Monaco
highlights.text: The editor, highlighting, file tree, icons and docking are custom-built in C#. No Monaco, Electron, embedded VS Code or screenshot-based UI is used.

highlights.title: Persistent rope text engine
highlights.text: A persistent AVL rope with indexed line navigation and structurally shared undo/redo, gated on two-million-character documents.

highlights.title: Multi-cursor editing
highlights.text: Multiple selections, Ctrl+D next-occurrence selection, Alt+Shift rectangular pointer selection, grapheme-aware deletion and literal/regex find and replace.

highlights.title: Folding and minimap
highlights.text: Folding with indexed visual rows, a minimap, whitespace visualization, line numbers and Ctrl+wheel font zoom.

highlights.title: Docked editor groups
highlights.text: Draggable tabs, nested horizontal/vertical editor splits and resizable side and bottom panels, backed by an immutable layout model.

highlights.title: Command palette and quick-open
highlights.text: Fuzzy commands with Ctrl+Shift+P, Go to file with Ctrl+P, breadcrumbs and workspace search.

highlights.title: VSIX extension host
highlights.text: Bounded VSIX inspection, explicit activation trust, browser worker and Node process hosts, with completion, hover, definition, symbol and format providers.

highlights.title: Batched Skia rendering
highlights.text: SKCanvasElement draws into Uno's Skia composition canvas with a 512-entry line layout cache and positioned-text batches.

items: Folding/unfolding with indexed visual rows
Multiple selections, next-occurrence selection and Alt+Shift rectangular pointer selection
Structurally shared undo/redo and version-checked atomic multi-document edits
Literal and regex find and replace, comments, autoindent and duplicate line
Suggestions, symbol navigation and Go to line/column
Minimap, line numbers, whitespace visualization, scrolling and zoom
Custom vector activity icons and a virtualized explorer
File create, import, rename, delete and export with dirty tab markers
Draggable tab reordering and moves across nested editor splits
Resizable side and bottom panels with Ctrl+B / Ctrl+J toggles
Fuzzy commands, quick-open, breadcrumbs, document status and workspace search
C#, JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON, Python, HTML and XML/XAML
CSS, Markdown, YAML, shell scripts and plain text
Stateful tokens, bracket diagnostics, folding ranges and declaration extraction
Incremental re-tokenization that stops once lexer state converges
Bounded, non-executing VSIX inspection with manifest/host classification
Explicit activation trust before any extension code runs
Bundled CommonJS loading in a browser module worker or an optional Node.js 22+ process
Completion, hover, definition, symbol and format providers bridged to the editor
Diagnostic collections with Problems entries and editor squiggles
Import UTF-8 text into a virtual workspace via File → Open / Import Files
Save/export the active file through a picker or download
Workspace: Export Backup writes a portable .codespace.json file
Local recovery of dirty baselines, selections, viewport and fold state
Live JSONC settings for font size, tab size, minimap, whitespace and line numbers
Draws into Uno's Skia composition canvas without a per-frame CPU bitmap upload
Up to 512 cached line layouts with positioned-text batches
Zero-allocation indexed line navigation on two-million-character documents
Fold mapping stored in proportion to collapsed intervals, not total lines

codeSamples.title: Edit text without any UI

playground.intro: The live build is the full C# workbench compiled to WebAssembly: import some files and try the editor, docking and command palette in your browser.

tour.title: Import a few files
tour.text: Use File → Open / Import Files to load UTF-8 text into the virtual workspace, then press Ctrl+P to jump between them.

tour.title: Drive it from the palette
tour.text: Press Ctrl+Shift+P (or F1) and run Fold All or Unfold All to collapse and reveal regions.

tour.title: Edit with multiple cursors
tour.text: Press Ctrl+D to add the next matching selection, or hold Alt+Shift and drag for a rectangular selection. Ctrl+H opens regex find and replace.

tour.title: Split the editor
tour.text: Press Ctrl+\ to split right, drag tabs between groups, and toggle the side bar and panel with Ctrl+B and Ctrl+J.

tour.title: Tweak settings live
tour.text: Edit the JSONC .vscode/settings.json to change font size, tab size, minimap or whitespace and see the editor update immediately.

tour.title: Back up your workspace
tour.text: Run Workspace: Export Backup to download everything as a portable .codespace.json file.

architecture.name: Text and workspace
architecture.text: Persistent AVL-rope text, a virtual workspace and transactional editor sessions with folding indexes.

architecture.name: Services
architecture.text: Lexical language services and an immutable split/tab docking model, all free of UI dependencies.

architecture.name: Extensions
architecture.text: Non-executing VSIX inspection and RPC framing in .NET, plus an independent JavaScript host for workers and Node.

architecture.name: Rendering
architecture.text: A SkiaSharp editor renderer that paints onto any caller-owned SKCanvas.

architecture.name: Uno workbench
architecture.text: Custom Uno controls composed into the embeddable WorkbenchView behind an IWorkbenchPlatform adapter.

boundaries: Development preview: not a complete or pixel-exact clone of Visual Studio Code
No LSP client, TextMate grammars, Git operations, real process terminal or debugger integration yet
Extensions are trusted executable code, not sandboxed; existing extensions work only within the API subset
Files live in a virtual workspace, not a watched disk folder; local recovery is not a backup
Full IME, bidi, contextual shaping, font fallback and screen-reader navigation remain open
